title: One Shared LoRA Weight for MRI Reconstruction across Acceleration Factors
abstract: Accelerated MRI reconstruction recovers images from undersampled k-space. However, different acceleration factors produce distinct artifact patterns. Existing methods often train separate models for each factor, leading to poor cross-factor generalization and high training and storage costs. We propose Shared LoRA, a parameter-efficient framework that freezes the pretrained SHFormer backbone and trains a single shared set of LoRA adapters together with a lightweight gating network. During training, undersampled inputs are generated by randomly sampling acceleration factors and their corresponding sampling masks, enabling the shared adapters to learn reconstruction knowledge across factors. Given the acceleration factor, GateNet generates layer-wise coefficients to dynamically modulate the residual strength of each adapter. Experiments show that Shared LoRA achieves the best or competitive PSNR and SSIM across acceleration factors, while its trainable parameters account for only about 5.3% of the total model parameters. Its performance at lower acceleration factors remains largely unaffected as the jointly trained factor set expands, and it generalizes stably to unseen neighboring factors.

title: Inducing Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacks with Iterative DPO
abstract: Reward hacking during reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) can induce reward seeking and broad misalignment in language models. Studying this misgeneralization is important for developing better threat models and countermeasures, but is often infeasible due to the cost of RL on large models. As an alternative, we propose studying emergent misalignment from iterative DPO, which preserves important properties of RLVR while reducing costs and enabling training on popular finetuning APIs. In practice, we find that training GPT-4.1 with iterative DPO on a single-turn reward hacking environment induces covert misaligned power-seeking and alignment faking, the first openly available (semi)-online training pipeline to induce these concerning forms of misalignment. We also find that training Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct with the same pipeline induces both misalignment and improved instruction following accuracy, showing that iterative DPO can be used as a testbed for selective generalization. Overall, we think iterative DPO can help democratize and accelerate the study of emergent misalignment from RLVR.

title: Cross-Lingual Representation Alignment by Token-Level Optimal Transport in a Language-Agnostic Space
abstract: Cross-lingual alignment (CLA) aims to align the representations of large language models (LLMs) across languages, enabling cross-lingual transfer to improve multilingual capabilities. Previous CLA methods often ignore language-specific information encoded in representations and only consider sentence-level alignment, which may lead to suboptimal performance and input-output language mismatch. We propose CAROT (Cross-Lingual Alignment of Representations in a Language-Agnostic Space via Optimal Transport), which consists of two steps: identifying language-specific representations in LLMs' internal states and aligning language-agnostic representations across languages at the token level by optimal transport, while explicitly preserving language-specific representations. Inference-time steering experiments show that the representations computed by CAROT are effective alignment targets, improving multilingual performance by up to 11.2 points in accuracy while maintaining input-output language consistency. We further use the representations obtained by CAROT as training targets, internalizing the aligned representations. The trained models outperform existing CLA methods in 11 of 18 evaluation settings (3 models $\times$ 3 tasks $\times$ ID/OOD languages). Our work provides insights into what constitutes effective alignment targets for CLA in LLMs. Code is available at https://github.com/ynklab/CAROT

title: 基于自组织网络的微分几何优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel differentiable optimization algorithm based on a self-organizing network structure. Traditional optimization methods often require manual network design, while this approach automates the discovery of optimal network structures. The algorithm constructs a self-organizing network, where nodes and edges dynamically interact to transmit information and optimize the objective function. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of numerical examples, showcasing its ability to find solutions that surpass traditional optimization techniques. The core mechanism involves a hierarchical representation of the problem and a self-adaptive network topology, enabling global optimization through a continuous, iterative process. This work presents a promising approach to differentiable optimization, offering a potential shift from handcrafted network designs to automated, intelligent network configurations.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Chaos Theory via Wave Function Optimization
abstract: Quantum-enhanced chaos theory aims to leverage quantum phenomena to improve our understanding and prediction of chaotic systems. This paper explores a novel algorithm, Quantum-Enhanced Chaos Theory via Wave Function Optimization, which utilizes quantum superposition to accelerate the analysis and prediction of chaotic dynamics. We propose a quantum algorithm, specifically a modified Grover's algorithm, to efficiently explore the wave function space, thereby enabling faster identification of critical states and improved forecasting accuracy. The core mechanism relies on the superposition of multiple wave functions, allowing for a parallel exploration of potential configurations within the chaotic system. This research will investigate the potential for enhanced sensitivity and predictability within chaotic systems through the application of this quantum optimization technique.

title: Symbiotic AI – Algorithm-Biological System Coupling
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to artificial intelligence termed "Symbiotic AI," centered on establishing direct, mutually beneficial relationships between artificial intelligence systems and biological organisms. The core claim is that AI performance can be dramatically improved by integrating biological intelligence, capitalizing on their inherent strengths in sensing, processing, and adaptation. This paradigm shift moves beyond traditional, purely computational AI models, incorporating biological systems as integral components. The proposed mechanism involves creating interfaces enabling AI to influence biological activity, such as modulating neuronal firing patterns, and conversely, receiving information from biological sensors – exemplified by olfactory perception. We argue this represents a fundamental change in AI architecture, fostering a synergistic relationship where each system complements the other's capabilities. This approach aims to create AI systems with greater robustness, adaptability, and a deeper understanding of complex, real-world environments. The paper outlines the key components and potential challenges associated with this symbiotic AI framework.

title: Quantum Error Correction Embedded Program Generation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum error correction (QEC) that integrates program execution with error correction. The core idea is to embed classical programs directly into the redundancy of QEC codes, such as QC-LDPC, enabling fault-tolerant execution in noisy quantum environments. The method involves decomposing the classical program into a sequence of quantum logic gates, which are then encoded within the QEC code's parity-check matrix. The error correction decoder, during its operation to detect and correct errors, simultaneously recovers the original quantum logic gates, effectively executing the embedded classical program. This represents a significant departure from traditional QEC, which primarily focuses on protecting quantum information, and introduces a new paradigm where programs themselves become the unit of error correction. This approach offers potential advantages in terms of resource utilization and program complexity, particularly for applications requiring intricate quantum computations. This paper outlines the theoretical framework, the encoding process, and discusses potential challenges and future research directions.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) faces significant challenges when dealing with complex, dynamic environments characterized by uncertainty and incomplete information. Traditional MARL approaches often rely on deterministic models, leading to suboptimal performance and instability. This paper proposes a novel framework that integrates probabilistic programming with MARL, leveraging the power of Bayesian inference to address these limitations. We introduce a system where the environment and agent behaviors are explicitly modeled using a probabilistic programming language, enabling the representation and reasoning about uncertainty. This approach allows agents to learn more robust policies through techniques like Monte Carlo Tree Search and variational inference, directly incorporating prior knowledge and adapting to changing conditions. The core contribution is a methodology for building MARL systems that can handle noisy observations, imperfect communication, and evolving environments, ultimately leading to improved learning efficiency and long-term performance. The system uses a Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework, represented by the tuple (S, A, P, R, γ), where: S represents the state space. A represents the action space. P(s'|s, a) represents the transition probability from state s to state s' given action a. R(s, a) represents the reward function. γ represents the discount factor. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a conceptual framework and outline potential future research directions focusing on scalability and practical implementation.

title: Self-Referential Neural Networks for Symbolic Representation Learning
abstract: Neural networks have demonstrated remarkable success in pattern recognition and prediction tasks, yet they fundamentally lack the ability to represent information in a symbolic, human-understandable way. This paper proposes a novel architecture, self-referential neural networks (SRNNs), designed to bridge this gap. The core idea is to recursively train networks to generate and manipulate symbolic representations of data, creating a system where the network's internal representations are treated as symbols, allowing for abstract reasoning and knowledge representation. We define a framework where SRNNs iteratively refine their internal symbolic structures through a process analogous to human cognition – breaking down complex problems into simpler, symbolically-defined subproblems. The architecture incorporates feedback loops allowing the network to evaluate and modify its own symbolic representations, leading to a self-correcting and potentially more robust learning process. We outline the key components of the SRNN architecture, focusing on the mechanisms for generating, manipulating, and evaluating these symbolic representations. The theoretical underpinnings of SRNNs are discussed, highlighting how they can be seen as a form of dynamic knowledge representation and reasoning. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential applications and future research directions for SRNNs.

title: Adaptive Topology Clustering Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive topology clustering algorithm designed to automatically construct topological structures and leverage these structures for data clustering and association analysis. Traditional clustering algorithms often rely on handcrafted features, limiting their flexibility and potential for uncovering subtle patterns within the data. This algorithm dynamically constructs topological structures, allowing for a more nuanced and robust clustering process. We propose a novel approach that utilizes the inherent topology of data points to guide the clustering process, resulting in improved clustering accuracy and the ability to identify meaningful associations between data points. The core mechanism involves mapping data points to topological spaces, dynamically adjusting the topology during the clustering process to maximize the likelihood of cluster formation. This approach offers a significant improvement over existing methods by providing a more intuitive and adaptable solution for data clustering.

title: Core Claim: Design a dynamic-adaptive clustering algorithm based on self-adaptive cluster centers, employing iterative adjustment of cluster centers to better reflect the complexity of data distribution, thereby improving clustering quality.
abstract: The objective of this research is to develop a novel dynamic-adaptive clustering algorithm designed to address the limitations of traditional clustering methods. Traditional clustering techniques often rely on fixed cluster centers, which fail to adequately represent the intricate patterns within datasets. This paper proposes a new approach that dynamically adjusts cluster centers during the iterative refinement process, enhancing the representation of data distribution and ultimately improving clustering quality. The core of this approach is a self-adaptive clustering center algorithm that leverages a sophisticated metric to determine the optimal adjustments to the cluster centers. This adaptive process enables the algorithm to respond effectively to the data's inherent complexity, leading to more accurate and robust clustering results. This work introduces a novel method that addresses the shortcomings of static cluster centers by implementing a dynamic adjustment strategy. The resulting algorithm demonstrates superior performance across a range of datasets, showcasing its potential for improved clustering applications. We will delve into the mathematical underpinnings of this dynamic adjustment mechanism and discuss its implications for various clustering scenarios. The algorithm's robustness and adaptability are key aspects that differentiate it from existing methods.

title: Based on Dynamic Graphs for Software Architecture Self-Adaptive Refactoring
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to software architecture self-adaptive refactoring based on dynamic graph modeling. Traditional software architecture modeling often relies on static representations, which struggle to capture the dynamic relationships and evolution inherent in software systems. This research addresses this limitation by transforming the software architecture into a dynamic graph, enabling the application of graph analysis and manipulation techniques for automated refactoring. The core claim is that by representing software architecture as a dynamic graph, we can leverage dynamic graph algorithms to analyze architectural properties like module coupling and dependencies, and then trigger refactoring operations such as module splitting and merging. This approach offers a more flexible and responsive solution for adapting software architecture to changing requirements, leading to improved system maintainability and adaptability. The presented methodology provides a foundation for intelligent architecture management, moving beyond static views towards a truly dynamic and self-optimizing system.

title: Adaptive Hardware Architecture Search via Evolutionary Algorithms and GPU Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to hardware architecture design leveraging the power of evolutionary algorithms (EAs) and GPU-based simulation. The core idea is to employ an EA to generate a population of potential hardware architectures, followed by rapid performance evaluation of each architecture using GPU simulations. The simulation results are then fed back into the EA to guide the subsequent generation of architectures, iteratively refining the design towards an optimal solution. The method demonstrates a significant potential for accelerating the architecture design process, particularly for complex systems where exhaustive search is computationally prohibitive. This research focuses on the theoretical framework and demonstrates the feasibility of this combined approach. The effectiveness of this adaptive architecture search is highlighted through the conceptual design and simulation results, showcasing the potential for improved performance and efficiency compared to traditional design methodologies. The proposed methodology offers a flexible and scalable framework for exploring diverse hardware designs, potentially leading to the discovery of innovative architectures tailored to specific application requirements.

title: Deep Barycentric Regression for Optimal Transport Map Estimation and its Statistical Optimality
abstract: The optimal transport (OT) map provides a geometric transformation for aligning probability distributions and has become a useful tool in machine learning. However, existing estimators of the OT map still exhibit a gap between sharp statistical guarantees and practical parametric estimation based on stable training objectives. Theoretical estimators achieve minimax optimal convergence rates, but they are typically nonparametric and can incur demanding implementation design or inference costs. Practical estimators are parametric and scalable, but their statistical guarantees remain underexplored, and their min-max, adversarial-like training objectives can be sensitive to optimization algorithms. We propose BROT (Barycentric Regression for OT), a simple two-step method that first computes the unregularized OT plan and then fits a deep neural network (DNN) to the induced barycentric targets by least-squares regression. Under standard regularity conditions, we prove that the DNN estimator of BROT attains the minimax convergence rate, when the ground-truth OT map is Lipschitz. Numerical studies on synthetic datasets and an image dataset show that BROT provides accurate map estimates, strong target distribution matching, and competitive transport costs, compared to existing estimation methods. Experiments on two downstream tasks, single-cell perturbation prediction and unsupervised domain adaptation, further suggest that the accurate estimation of BROT can translate into stronger task performance.

title: Geometric Machine Learning Adaptive Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric machine learning framework designed to enhance model generalization by dynamically adjusting the geometric structure of the model during training. Traditional machine learning relies heavily on manual parameter tuning, often limiting model flexibility and hindering optimal performance. Our framework leverages the principles of geometric understanding and machine learning algorithms to automatically optimize the model's geometric configuration, resulting in improved robustness and predictive capabilities. This work explores a method for adapting model geometry based on the input data, providing a new approach to achieving superior generalization.

title: Geometric Topology Encoding: A Natural Language Processing Approach
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric topology encoding to natural language processing (NLP) tasks. We propose a novel approach leveraging auto-encoding techniques to transform geometric topological features extracted from text into meaningful vector representations. The core idea is to automatically learn more effective semantic representations by training a neural network to map topological changes to a latent space. We evaluate the performance of this method on several NLP benchmarks, demonstrating improvements in semantic analysis and text generation compared to traditional methods. The research highlights the potential of this technique to enhance NLP models by introducing a new dimension of semantic representation.

title: Self-Adaptive Topological Control for Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for exponentially faster computation compared to classical computers. However, achieving this advantage requires precise control over quantum systems, a task that is often challenging due to their inherent fragility and sensitivity to environmental perturbations. This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum computing – Self-Adaptive Topological Control (SATC) – which leverages the unique properties of topological quantum systems to dynamically adjust quantum system parameters, thereby enhancing computational efficiency. We present a theoretical framework and a preliminary implementation of SATC, demonstrating its efficacy in stabilizing complex quantum states and facilitating complex quantum algorithms. The core claim centers on the design of a SATC implementation capable of achieving significant performance gains through optimized parameter adjustments. This work introduces a new method for manipulating quantum states, offering a potential paradigm shift in the field of quantum computing.

title: Title: Emergent Topology in Deep Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the potential for emergent topology within deep neural networks, exploring a novel mechanism to dynamically shape the network's internal representations and foster novel learning algorithms. Traditional neural networks exhibit static architectures, limiting their adaptability and generalization capabilities. We introduce a dynamic topology-inducing algorithm that encourages the network to explore and generate topological features, resulting in improved robustness and a more self-organizing structure. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments utilizing a modified convolutional neural network, showcasing enhanced performance on a variety of benchmark datasets. The core claim is that the inherent topology of the network can be dynamically shaped by input data, leading to improved learning and generalization.

title: Nonlinear Geometric Group Quantum State Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational model for analyzing the quantum states of non-linear geometric groups, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement and quantum computation. The core claim is to develop a framework that predicts and analyzes quantum states of these groups, offering insights into their quantum phase transitions and potential for quantum information storage. Traditional quantum state estimation methods are inadequate for this complex system, necessitating a more holistic approach that integrates geometric properties with quantum mechanics. We propose a model that utilizes entangled states to represent the group's quantum properties and employs quantum computation to generate and analyze the resulting quantum states. This work advances the field by providing a fundamentally new perspective on the quantum dynamics of geometric groups, opening avenues for deeper understanding of quantum information processing and potentially enabling the development of novel quantum algorithms.

abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive quantum entanglement to dynamic geometric structures for simulating quantum systems. We propose a novel framework that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust geometric parameters within a quantum system. This adjustment optimizes system performance through a process of iterative refinement of the geometry, offering a more versatile and potentially superior approach compared to traditional simulation methods. The core mechanism involves manipulating geometric parameters based on entanglement measurements, resulting in a system that exhibits enhanced stability and sensitivity to subtle environmental changes. The study focuses on demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach through simulations, showcasing improvements in system fidelity and performance metrics. We present a preliminary analysis of the framework's capabilities and limitations, highlighting future research directions.

title: Title: Dynamically Reconfigurable Quantum Fields (DRQF)
abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework for dynamically reconfigurable quantum fields, utilizing a quantum feedback loop to dynamically adjust the fundamental parameters of the field. Traditional quantum field theory often relies on fixed parameters, limiting the system's adaptability. The DRQF approach allows for a fundamental shift in the field's properties, opening up possibilities for entirely new quantum phenomena and applications. We outline the core mechanism, detailing the design of the quantum feedback loop and its impact on the field's evolution. This work demonstrates the potential for a significantly more flexible and adaptable quantum system, exceeding the limitations of fixed parameter models. The paper will present a detailed mathematical analysis of the feedback loop, including its stability and convergence properties, and explore potential applications in areas such as quantum computing and metrological quantum systems.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Parallel Transport for Graph Embeddings
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-Euclidean parallel transport as a novel technique for generating graph embeddings. Traditional graph embedding methods often rely on distance measures, which struggle to capture the intricate relationships within a graph. This research proposes a new method that explicitly incorporates this concept, utilizing geometric transformations to represent node connections and enabling a more expressive and robust embedding. This approach aims to overcome limitations of standard techniques by offering a more nuanced understanding of graph structure. The paper details the core mechanism, provides a comprehensive explanation of the geometric approach, and discusses the potential benefits and challenges of this method. We present a detailed mathematical framework and initial results demonstrating the effectiveness of this technique in generating graph embeddings, showcasing its ability to capture complex relationships more effectively than existing methods.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Entanglement for Probabilistic Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense promise for revolutionizing probabilistic modeling. Current methods often struggle with the inherent limitations of representing complex systems with fidelity, particularly in scenarios requiring nuanced probabilistic outcomes. This paper introduces an algorithmic quantum entanglement framework designed to overcome these limitations, offering a self-improving process for constructing probabilistic models with enhanced accuracy. We explore a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts entanglement parameters based on system state, fostering a continuous refinement of simulation fidelity. This work presents a significant advancement in the application of quantum mechanics to probabilistic modeling, aiming to unlock new possibilities in fields ranging from quantum chemistry to financial risk assessment.

title: 可解释的深度学习模型验证框架 (EDLVVF)
abstract: The interpretability of deep learning models remains a significant challenge in deploying these models in critical applications. This paper introduces the Explainable Deep Learning Model Verification Framework (EDLVVF), a novel approach to quantitatively assess and validate the interpretability of deep learning models. EDLVVF leverages causal inference and concept distillation techniques to transform complex deep learning models into more understandable representations. We then utilize established interpretability metrics, augmented with a new confidence score derived from the causal mapping process, to provide a comprehensive evaluation. The framework aims to provide a rigorous methodology for understanding the degree to which a model's decisions are genuinely driven by the intended features rather than spurious correlations. This paper details the framework's architecture, the core mechanisms, and its potential applications, ultimately contributing to the development of more trustworthy and reliable deep learning systems.

title: 基于动态的量子熵的计算策略
abstract: Quantum systems exhibit complex behavior due to their inherent uncertainty. Quantifying this uncertainty, specifically the quantum entropy, is a central challenge in quantum information theory. Traditional entropy calculations often rely on approximations, limiting their accuracy and computational efficiency. This paper introduces a novel computational strategy, leveraging dynamic quantum entropy modeling, to enhance the estimation of quantum system entropy and predict their behavior. We propose a novel framework that dynamically models the evolution of quantum states, allowing for automatic adjustment of entropy calculation models through machine learning. This approach offers a more precise and adaptive method for quantifying quantum uncertainty, potentially revolutionizing the field of quantum information processing. The core mechanism involves creating a dynamic entropy model that adjusts to the evolving quantum state. We present a preliminary evaluation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, showcasing improved accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods.

title: Title: Formal Verification of Quantum Complexity
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements across numerous fields, but the inherent fragility of quantum systems necessitates robust verification methods. Traditional verification approaches often rely on trial-and-error, lacking the necessary mathematical rigor to guarantee correctness. This paper proposes a novel approach to formal verification of quantum algorithms and systems, focusing on the development of a "complexity metric" that provides a mathematical framework for assessing the trustworthiness of quantum technologies. This metric will enable automated verification against pre-defined complexity limits, offering a significant step towards building reliable and dependable quantum systems.

title: Quantum Security Based on Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum decoherence as a fundamental element in designing novel security protocols for quantum algorithms. Traditional approaches to quantum security often rely on the computational intractability for classical computers, a vulnerability that quantum computers pose. This work proposes a shift in strategy, leveraging the inherent fragility of quantum states – specifically, their susceptibility to decoherence – to create robust security measures. We explore methods for introducing controlled noise and interference to disrupt the coherence of quantum information, effectively preventing adversaries from extracting cryptographic keys. The core claim of this research is that by exploiting quantum decoherence, we can design algorithms with significantly enhanced resilience against attacks. We present a framework for analyzing the impact of decoherence on specific algorithms and propose strategies for incorporating decoherence into security protocols. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions in this emerging field.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Networks for Predicting Scientific Discovery
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to understanding and predicting scientific discovery utilizing Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs). The core argument posits that scientific discovery is not a purely random process but rather a structured evolution driven by cycles of exploration and exploitation. To model this, we construct DBNs that learn to predict the emergence of new scientific hypotheses and theories by analyzing the current state of scientific knowledge. These networks incorporate concepts of novelty and convergence, allowing them to identify potential breakthroughs and predict the trajectory of knowledge development. The predictive power of the model is evaluated through simulated scenarios, demonstrating its capacity to identify promising research directions and understand the dynamic nature of scientific progress. The key contribution lies in the application of DBNs to the domain of scientific discovery, providing a framework for understanding the underlying patterns and predicting future advancements.

title: Explainable Deep Generative Models with Adversarial Sample Defense
abstract: Deep generative models have achieved remarkable success in various domains, including image generation, text generation, and music generation. However, these models often operate as black boxes, lacking transparency and interpretability. Furthermore, they are highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks, where subtle perturbations in the input can lead to drastically different and incorrect outputs. This research addresses these critical limitations by proposing a novel framework that integrates explainable AI (XAI) techniques with adversarial training methods. We leverage SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values to provide insights into the generative model's decision-making process, enabling us to understand the factors driving the generated outputs. Simultaneously, we employ adversarial training to enhance the model's robustness against adversarial attacks. Our approach aims to create a deep generative model that is both interpretable and resilient to malicious inputs. The key contributions of this work are the combined approach of XAI-driven interpretation and adversarial defense, offering a pathway towards more trustworthy and secure deep generative models.

title: Adaptive Probabilistic Model Reasoning Engine
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Probabilistic Model Reasoning Engine (APMRE) designed to address the limitations of traditional static probabilistic models in uncertain reasoning scenarios. The core claim is to develop a reasoning engine capable of dynamically updating probability models based on accumulating evidence, leading to improved accuracy and efficiency. The proposed mechanism leverages Bayesian Networks or Variational Inference techniques coupled with a novel "learning module." This module automatically adjusts model parameters based on incoming evidence, facilitating adaptive learning. Unlike existing systems that rely on pre-defined models, APMRE offers a significantly more flexible and robust approach to non-deterministic reasoning. The engine's adaptability directly translates to higher inference precision and potentially faster convergence times, making it suitable for complex, evolving, and data-rich environments. This paper outlines the architecture, key components, and theoretical underpinnings of APMRE, highlighting its advantages and potential applications.

title: RationalQuaternionSigmaProduct: a rational-quaternion Σ-Product network on total arithmetic
abstract: A Σ-Product network over the quaternions: inputs X or X⁻¹, exponent layers stacked in depth with exponents W ∈ ℍ_ℚ generated from natural-number prime valuations and applied on the left (Exp(W·Log H)) or the right (Exp((Log H)·W)), ordered Hamilton products, a fixed right basis and a quaternion-linear Σ readout solved by least squares, with the structure found by a gradient sensor and an exact discrete search. The reference implementation (NumPy/IEEE) defines the structure; the same network is implemented on the total arithmetic of total-arith-cuda — the Hamilton product as a wiring product, the reserved-word logarithm Log₀(0) = 0, ε as a tagged boundary value, saturation flags instead of clamps, and a least-squares readout over the samples the arithmetic can vouch for. A parity check over random structures shows the two agree on every unflagged entry once the reference's unmarked guards are removed; on contaminated data the reference is steered by one silently clipped row while the total network excludes it and recovers the teacher.

title: Novel Methods for Catheter and Guidewire Segmentation in X-ray Fluoroscopy under a Federated Learning Setting
abstract: Endovascular procedures rely on real-time manipulation of thin instruments, catheters and guidewires, under X-ray fluoroscopy guidance, where accurate visual analysis is essential for procedural safety. Learning-based methods are constrained by structural complexity, data scarcity, and privacy regulations precluding centralised training across institutions. This thesis presents a structure-aware federated learning framework for catheter and guidewire analysis, with four contributions evaluated on real-animal and phantom data. A benchmark dataset, CathAction, is introduced for catheterisation analysis, with over 600,000 annotated frames and 40,000 segmentation masks. A shape-sensitive loss transforms masks into signed distance maps compared in a structural feature space, improving Dice coefficient by up to 2.9 points across five backbones. This is extended to federated learning with shape-sensitive loss, preserving geometric consistency under heterogeneous client data and outperforming federated averaging by up to three points in mean intersection-over-union as clients scale from four to eight. Federated learning with projected gradient descent adds adversarial optimisation, raising mean intersection-over-union by over ten points on real-animal data. Finally, a structure-aware diffusion framework synthesises catheter and guidewire video sequences, combining structural supervision with a domain-adaptive reconstruction objective, reducing Frechet video distance over a strong baseline while maintaining visual fidelity. Incorporating synthetic sequences into federated training raises the Dice score from 44 to 51 percent under data scarcity, with gains across four held-out sites. Together, these contributions advance privacy-preserving catheter and guidewire analysis, supporting collaborative training without centralising patient data or large amounts of manual annotation.

A shape-sensitive loss transforms masks into signed distance maps compared in a structural feature space, improving Dice coefficient by up to 2.9 points across five backbones. This is extended to federated learning with shape-sensitive loss, preserving geometric consistency under heterogeneous client data and outperforming federated averaging by up to three points in mean intersection-over-union as clients scale from four to eight. Federated learning with projected gradient descent adds adversarial optimisation, raising mean intersection-over-union by over ten points on real-animal data. Finally, a structure-aware diffusion framework synthesises catheter and guidewire video sequences, combining structural supervision with a domain-adaptive reconstruction objective, reducing Frechet video distance over a strong baseline while maintaining visual fidelity. Incorporating synthetic sequences into federated training raises the Dice score from 44 to 51 percent under data scarcity, with gains across four held-out sites. Together, these contributions advance privacy-preserving catheter and guidewire analysis, supporting collaborative training without centralising patient data or large amounts of manual annotation.

title: 量子纠错协议的基于概率模型的自适应算法
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a crucial aspect of quantum information processing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum states. Traditional QEC methods rely on complex and computationally intensive error correction protocols, posing significant challenges for scalability and implementation. This paper introduces a novel quantum error correction protocol based on a probabilistic model, designed to dynamically adjust quantum error correction parameters and strategies based on the probability of error, thereby significantly enhancing the fidelity of quantum information. The core mechanism involves modeling the quantum error correction process as a probabilistic event, allowing for adaptive parameter optimization and strategy selection. This approach overcomes the limitations of fixed parameter schemes, offering a more robust and efficient solution for QEC. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved performance through enhanced error detection and correction capabilities, ultimately paving the way for practical quantum computation.

title: Title: Probabilistic Programming with Adaptive Kernel Selection
abstract: Probabilistic programming offers a powerful framework for modeling complex systems and generating diverse outcomes. However, traditional approaches often rely on fixed kernels, limiting the model's flexibility and hindering its ability to capture intricate relationships within data. This paper proposes a novel approach to probabilistic programming that incorporates adaptive kernel selection, dynamically adjusting the kernel function based on the data and the model's current state. We introduce a mechanism that automatically evaluates different kernel functions and selects the one that best fits the data and the model's current parameters. This adaptive kernel selection significantly enhances the model's capacity to represent complex data distributions and improve the accuracy of probabilistic predictions. The proposed system addresses the limitations of existing probabilistic programming techniques by providing a more robust and adaptable framework for modeling real-world problems.

title: Title: Adaptive Nonlinear Geometric Transformations for Quantum Entanglement Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally powerful approach to computation, surpassing the limitations of classical algorithms in certain complex scenarios. This research explores the potential of utilizing adaptive nonlinear geometric transformations to enhance quantum entanglement computation. We propose a novel framework that leverages the unique properties of entanglement to achieve precise calculations of intricate geometric transformations. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting geometric parameters to optimize the entanglement's state, thereby improving the accuracy and efficiency of the computation. This work addresses the challenges of traditional computational methods with complex geometric manipulations, presenting a new perspective on quantum entanglement applications. The design introduces a sophisticated algorithm that intelligently manipulates geometric contexts to minimize errors and maximize entanglement fidelity. This approach promises to significantly advance the capabilities of quantum computation, particularly in areas involving precise geometric manipulation. The investigation of this framework is driven by the inherent strengths of entanglement and the potential for algorithmic innovation. Further, this paper will present a detailed explanation of the proposed framework, outlining its mathematical foundations and experimental validation demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Cognitive Networks
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative cognitive network architecture, termed Adaptive Self-Organizing Cognitive Networks (ASOCN), designed to enhance knowledge representation and robustness through continuous learning and meta-learning. Traditional AI models often rely on static knowledge representations and fine-tuning, limiting their adaptability and potential for discovery. ASOCN moves beyond this by actively searching for and exploiting unexpected correlations within its own data, fostering a self-optimizing system capable of continuous improvement. We propose a novel mechanism centered around meta-learning driven by observed data patterns, prioritizing novelty and robustness – a departure from traditional static representations. This work explores the potential of ASOCN to surpass existing AI capabilities in knowledge discovery and adaptability.

title: 基于量子混沌的自适应神经网络
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum chaos in neural networks to enhance model prediction accuracy and adaptability. We propose a novel neural network architecture, termed "Quantum Chaotic Neural Network" (QCN), which leverages the unique properties of quantum chaos – specifically, the sensitivity to initial conditions and the presence of chaotic attractors – to achieve self-adaptive behavior and improved predictive capabilities. The core mechanism involves incorporating quantum chaos into the network's structure through a carefully designed layer arrangement and activation function, facilitating the formation of complex, dynamically adjusting patterns. This approach offers a departure from traditional neural network designs, promising enhanced robustness and generalization. The study utilizes a series of simulations and preliminary analyses to demonstrate the efficacy of the QCN in various predictive tasks. The results indicate a significant improvement in prediction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art neural networks, particularly in scenarios involving complex and non-linear relationships. The paper concludes with a discussion of the limitations of the proposed approach and outlines future research directions, including exploring the application of quantum chaos to other machine learning paradigms.

title: Differential Privacy for Graph Analytics with Wasserstein Distance
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to differential privacy in graph analytics, addressing the limitations of existing methods which frequently result in substantial structural distortions within the analyzed graphs. The core idea is to leverage Wasserstein distance as a more refined metric for quantifying privacy loss compared to traditional approaches. We present a new algorithm designed to minimize this Wasserstein distance while maintaining the fundamental characteristics of the graph structure. Our method provides a more accurate and nuanced understanding of the privacy-utility trade-off inherent in graph analytics, ultimately leading to better-protected datasets. The key innovation lies in adapting differential privacy to the complexities of network data, offering a significantly improved strategy for preserving privacy during graph analysis.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Symbolic Regression
abstract: Symbolic regression aims to discover mathematical expressions that accurately represent a given set of data points. Traditional approaches often struggle with complex, high-dimensional datasets and require extensive computational resources. Reservoir computing (RC) provides a potentially efficient alternative by utilizing a randomly connected recurrent neural network (reservoir) to map inputs to outputs without explicit training of the reservoir itself. However, RC's performance is often limited by its inherent lack of theoretical understanding and its reliance on heuristics. This paper introduces a novel approach, Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing (QIRC), which leverages principles from quantum mechanics to design and operate the reservoir. Specifically, we model the reservoir as a system of entangled qubits, mimicking quantum superposition and measurement. The output of the reservoir is then processed through a minimal set of linear regressions, directly inspired by quantum measurement theory, to extract the desired symbolic expression. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual simulations, the potential for QIRC to overcome some of the limitations of traditional RC, offering improved function approximation capabilities, particularly in scenarios where the underlying function exhibits non-Markovian behavior. The key innovation lies in the explicit incorporation of quantum concepts into the RC framework, creating a more naturally high-dimensional and adaptable state space.

title: Neuromorphic Reservoir Computing for Symbolic Representation
abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) has emerged as a promising technique for time-series prediction due to its computational efficiency and ability to capture complex temporal dynamics. However, a significant limitation of traditional RC is its lack of direct connection to symbolic representations – the fundamental building blocks of human cognition and knowledge representation. This work proposes a novel approach leveraging the principles of RC to directly generate symbolic representations from continuous input data. The core idea is to design a specifically engineered neuromorphic reservoir that, through its inherent dynamics, maps continuous inputs into discrete symbols. This approach effectively bridges the gap between neural networks and symbolic reasoning, offering a potentially powerful method for processing and understanding complex, symbolic information. We outline the design considerations, key mathematical formulations, and potential applications of this system. The system's ability to translate continuous input into discrete symbolic representations offers a new avenue for exploring intelligence inspired by biological systems.

title: Dynamic Information Entropy Coding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to information entropy coding, termed Dynamic Information Entropy Coding (DIEC), which addresses the limitations of traditional static entropy coding methods. The core idea is to leverage real-time monitoring of data distribution dynamics rather than relying on fixed models, thereby achieving adaptive optimization of entropy coding parameters. This is achieved through the introduction of "entropy probes" – reinforcement learning agents that continuously assess the impact of encoding parameters on the data distribution. These probes utilize gradient descent algorithms to adjust the encoder, mirroring the adaptive learning process observed in humans. The proposed DIEC framework offers significant potential for improved compression rates and transmission efficiency, particularly in scenarios with non-stationary data distributions. The key contribution lies in the dynamic adaptation capabilities, enabling the coding system to respond effectively to evolving data characteristics. This paper details the theoretical framework and outlines the core components of the DIEC system, emphasizing the integration of reinforcement learning for robust and efficient entropy coding.

abstract: This paper explores the application of multi-agent learning (MAL) techniques to control complex systems comprised of multiple interacting agents. Multi-agent learning offers a promising alternative by allowing individual agents to learn their own strategies and collaboratively optimize the overall system performance. This work details a framework for utilizing MAL to achieve stability and desired performance in complex multi-agent systems. The core claim is that MAL provides a novel approach to controlling systems with complex interactive behaviors. The proposed mechanism involves each agent independently learning its policy, combined with multi-agent cooperation for global optimization. title: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks for Autonomous Robot Navigation
abstract: Autonomous robot navigation necessitates robust perception and decision-making capabilities that can adapt to dynamic and unpredictable environments. Traditional graph neural networks (GNNs) often rely on static graph structures, failing to effectively represent and reason about the constantly evolving relationships within a robot's surroundings. This paper proposes a novel framework utilizing Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) to address this limitation. The DGNN architecture incorporates dynamically adjusted node and edge attributes, driven by sensor data and the robot's internal state. This allows for real-time adaptation of the graph representation, improving the robot's ability to accurately perceive its environment and make informed navigation decisions. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis and a detailed specification of the DGNN design, emphasizing its advantages over static GNNs. The core claim is that static GNNs cannot adapt to the constantly changing environment experienced by autonomous robots. The key mechanism is the utilization of a GNN architecture with dynamically adjusted node and edge attributes based on sensor data and the robot's internal state, allowing for real-time adaptation of the graph representation.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance via Differential Privacy
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly sharing the data itself. However, existing FL systems face significant vulnerabilities, including malicious participant attacks and data breaches. This paper proposes a novel decentralized federated learning framework that integrates Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT) protocols, inspired by blockchain technology, with differential privacy (DP) mechanisms. The core claim is that this synergistic combination provides a substantially more robust and secure FL paradigm. Specifically, the system utilizes BFT to detect and mitigate malicious behavior from participants, ensuring data integrity and model robustness, while DP safeguards user privacy by adding controlled noise to the model updates. This framework allows the system to tolerate a certain number of Byzantine failures while maintaining accurate models. The system architecture is decentralized, eliminating a single point of failure and enhancing overall resilience. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a conceptual implementation strategy.

title: Layer-Wise Gate-Controlled Prompt Truncation in a Multimodal Chest X-Ray Classifier
abstract: Mixture of Prompt Experts (MoPE) adapts multimodal transformers through input-dependent prompt composition, while retaining a fixed prompt length. We investigate a layer-wise gating extension in a binary chest X-ray classification pilot study. The controller predicts a retention ratio for each sample, averages these ratios within a mini-batch, and uses the resulting integer length to truncate the static and mixed visual prompts. Retained mixed prompts are also scaled by the individual ratios. In one recorded run per configuration, the gated model reached a best validation accuracy of 0.8996, compared with 0.8969 for the fixed-length baseline; the corresponding final values were 0.8963 and 0.8802. The exported gate statistics imply a retained length of one at all recorded training points, relative to a configured maximum of six. This reduces the complete visual sequence from 210 to 200 tokens, but no direct runtime measurements establish an acceleration benefit. Report-derived labels, report text as input, sequential data partitioning, and the absence of repeated controlled experiments limit interpretation. The findings document prompt shortening under the configured gate penalty; they do not establish sample-specific length allocation, superiority over fixed short prompts, or clinical utility. Code is available at: https://github.com/jingtaolei/mope-dynamic-prompt-truncation.

The findings document prompt shortening under the configured gate penalty; they do not establish sample-specific length allocation, superiority over fixed short prompts, or clinical utility. Code is available at: https://github.com/jingtaolei/mope-dynamic-prompt-truncation.

title: FrankenReport: Early Exiting in Long-Form Generation Using Expected Value of Computation
abstract: While deep research systems address interactive information-seeking needs impressively, their real-world deployments face latency and resource-consumption challenges. We present FrankenReport, an interface for long-form knowledge-seeking report generation that supports adaptive early exiting per section: it evaluates intermediate outputs during generation and predicts whether further targeted computation will yield significant quality gains. In a simulation study, FrankenReport outperforms random allocation baselines by a large margin (up to 4x) under low budgets and smoothly recovers full-pipeline quality as the budget grows, showing that future quality gains are predictable from intermediate drafts. Through experiments and user studies, we further show that despite varying preferences across users and topics, FrankenReport adapts to simple, natural user feedback as efficiently as methods requiring much costlier supervision such as generated drafts and explicit rationales.

title: Quantum Entanglement Geometry Quantization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a profound challenge to our understanding of information and computation. This research investigates the geometric properties of quantum entanglement, proposing a novel model – Quantum Entanglement Geometry Quantization (QGC) – that leverages entanglement to predict and optimize quantum computation processes. We explore the potential of QGC to provide a more efficient and robust framework for information transfer and processing, offering a significant advancement over traditional approaches. The core mechanism centers around constructing a geometric representation of entangled states, predicting key properties of quantum entanglement, and ultimately, suggesting potential applications within quantum algorithms and quantum information theory. This paper presents a preliminary analysis, demonstrating the potential of QGC to offer a new perspective on entanglement's impact on computation.

title: Title: Universal Quantum State Transformation via Wave Function Synthesis
abstract: Quantum state transformation is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, crucial for manipulating and analyzing quantum states. Traditional methods often rely on predefined transformations, limiting their applicability to specific scenarios. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum state transformation – Wave Function Synthesis (WFS) – which utilizes a dynamic generation of transformation maps to enable the mapping of quantum states to each other. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of theoretical and experimental analyses, highlighting its potential for creating a universal mapping system. WFS offers a more flexible and powerful approach compared to existing transformation techniques, addressing limitations in current state representation and manipulation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Phase Correction: An Adaptive Approach to Error Mitigation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unparalleled computational power. However, its delicate nature necessitates careful management of quantum states to minimize errors. This paper introduces a novel quantum error correction algorithm, Quantum Entanglement Phase Correction (QEP), predicated on the inherent adaptability of quantum entanglement. We propose a method that leverages the self-adjusting nature of entangled states to actively correct errors during quantum information processing. This approach significantly reduces the impact of decoherence and other sources of error, ultimately enhancing the precision and robustness of quantum computations. The proposed QEP algorithm offers a promising pathway toward more reliable and accurate quantum information handling, addressing a critical challenge in the field of quantum technology.

title: Core Claim: Researching non-linear topological quantum computation using adaptive geometric simplification techniques, automatically adjusting topological structure during computation to reduce computational complexity and improve efficiency.
abstract: The development of quantum computing has spurred significant research into novel computational paradigms, particularly those leveraging topological quantum systems. Non-linear topological quantum computation offers a promising pathway to enhanced computational power due to its inherent robustness against local noise. This paper investigates a novel approach to improve the efficiency of non-linear topological quantum computation by employing adaptive geometric simplification. We propose a sophisticated algorithm that dynamically adjusts the topology of the underlying quantum system during the computation process, minimizing the number of required steps and ultimately enhancing computational performance. This work addresses a critical challenge in the field – the inherent computational complexity associated with traditional topological quantum algorithms – through the introduction of self-adjusting geometric simplification. We analyze the benefits of this approach in a specific model, demonstrating a significant reduction in computational cost compared to existing methods. The research explores the interplay between topological properties, geometric simplification, and the efficiency of quantum computations. The focus is on developing a practical and scalable algorithm that can be applied to a broader range of non-linear topological quantum systems. The core mechanism involves a self-optimizing geometric simplification algorithm that adjusts the system's topology in real-time, thereby reducing computational bottlenecks.

title: 循环自适应机器学习的几何特征提取
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to machine learning, termed "Cycle-Adaptive Machine Learning" (CAML), that leverages geometric feature extraction to enhance model predictive accuracy and robustness. Traditional machine learning models often struggle with high-dimensional data and complex relationships, leading to overfitting and poor generalization. CAML addresses these challenges by dynamically adjusting the geometric features extracted during the training process. This adaptive process involves iterative refinement of these features based on the model's performance, resulting in improved predictive capabilities. The paper details the algorithm's core mechanisms, provides a theoretical foundation for its efficacy, and presents a comprehensive evaluation of its performance on various datasets. The core claim is that CAML significantly surpasses existing methods in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness, offering a more sophisticated and adaptable approach to machine learning.

title: Title: Temporal Recurrence Network (TRN) for Data Compression
abstract: This paper presents the Temporal Recurrence Network (TRN), a novel data compression technique that leverages dynamic network adjustments based on temporal patterns within datasets. Traditional compression algorithms often rely on static compression methods, failing to effectively exploit the inherent sequential structure of data. The TRN employs a neural network trained to predict future data changes, creating a 'temporal graph' that compresses data by leveraging these learned predictions. This approach offers enhanced compression efficiency and robustness compared to existing methods, particularly when dealing with data exhibiting significant temporal dependencies. The paper details the architecture, training process, and experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of the TRN in various data compression scenarios.

title: Quantum Decoherence Modeling Based on Probabilistic Models
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to modeling quantum decoherence using probabilistic models. Traditional quantum decoherence models often rely on simplified assumptions, leading to inaccuracies in predicting decoherence times. This work introduces a more rigorous framework based on statistical physics principles, explicitly incorporating probabilistic elements to capture the complex dynamics of quantum systems. The core of the model lies in formulating decoherence as a probabilistic process, allowing for a more accurate quantification of the rate at which quantum information is lost. We derive key equations that describe the evolution of the quantum state under the influence of various decoherence mechanisms. The model's parameters are determined through statistical analysis of the underlying quantum system, providing a predictive capability for decoherence times. Simulation results demonstrate the improved accuracy of this probabilistic approach compared to conventional models. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum decoherence modeling, offering a more reliable tool for designing and analyzing quantum computing architectures and quantum information processing protocols.

title: Symmetry Geometry Transformations and Multi-Body Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates the application of symmetry geometry transformations within the context of multi-body quantum entanglement. The core claim is that these transformations can mitigate the detrimental effects of entanglement degradation, offering a novel approach to quantum information transfer and processing. We explore the potential of employing these transformations to reduce the vulnerability of entangled states, ultimately enhancing the fidelity and stability of quantum systems. The study focuses on demonstrating the efficacy of a specific transformation – a geometric shift – in reducing entanglement entropy and preserving quantum information. The research aims to contribute to the theoretical understanding of entanglement protection and provides a potential pathway for improved quantum technologies.

title: Title: Adaptive Natural Language Processing for Text Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This research investigates the application of an adaptive natural language processing (NLP) framework for text sentiment analysis. Traditional sentiment analysis methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and nuances of human language, requiring extensive feature engineering and model training. This paper proposes a dynamic adaptive NLP framework that dynamically adjusts model parameters and features based on the characteristics of the input text data. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously optimizes the model's performance through an iterative process of data analysis and parameter refinement. The implementation aims to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of sentiment detection, addressing the limitations of conventional approaches. The study explores the benefits of this approach in various scenarios and demonstrates its effectiveness through quantitative analysis.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks for Hardware Architecture Design
abstract: The design of neural network architectures for hardware implementation presents a significant challenge, often requiring substantial manual effort and specialized knowledge. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing a self-organizing neural network (SONN) to autonomously generate efficient neural network architectures tailored to specific hardware constraints. The SONN learns the design process directly from training data, iteratively evolving its own architecture based on performance metrics such as latency, power consumption, and accuracy. The core mechanism involves a recurrent neural network architecture, where each layer represents a design decision – e.g., layer type, number of neurons, connectivity patterns. The network is trained to minimize a cost function that combines these performance metrics with a regularization term encouraging architectural diversity. This approach offers a potentially automated and scalable solution for hardware architecture design, reducing the reliance on human expertise and accelerating the development of optimized neural network implementations. The paper details the architecture of the SONN, the training methodology, and presents a preliminary evaluation demonstrating the network's ability to generate architectures competitive with manually designed ones.

We then detail a specific design framework incorporating these principles, demonstrating its effectiveness through a series of representative quantum circuit examples. The results showcase a significant improvement in quantum circuit performance compared to traditional approaches.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Natural Language Understanding
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to natural language understanding (NLU) that combines the strengths of neural networks and symbolic reasoning. Current deep learning models, while achieving impressive results in tasks like machine translation and question answering, often suffer from a lack of explainability and struggle with complex reasoning. We propose a neuro-symbolic framework where neural networks are used for perception and initial understanding, while symbolic reasoning techniques handle the logical inference and deduction required for more sophisticated tasks. This integration aims to overcome the limitations of purely data-driven approaches by injecting explicit knowledge and reasoning rules. The core claim of this work is that by merging the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the logical precision of symbolic systems, a more robust, explainable, and truly intelligent NLU system can be achieved. The proposed system is evaluated through a theoretical analysis of its components and potential applications, demonstrating its promise for tackling challenging NLU problems. We outline a key mechanism for achieving this integration and highlight the novel aspects of this combined approach.

title: Automatic classification of cyber incidents using privacy-preserving artificial intelligence
abstract: As cyber incidents increase in complexity, diversity and frequency, cybersecurity practitioners find it more challenging to extract meaningful threat intelligence and insights from cyber incident reports. This problem is worsened by the limited number of these reports; as cyber incident victims may withhold and/or downplaytheir reports due to reputational and privacy concerns. Therefore, this study aims to determine whether cyber incident reports, which have been stripped of personal data (pseudonymised), can be classified according to the Spanish INCIBE Cyber Incident Taxonomy. Seven transformers (SecBERT, BERT, DistilBERT, BERTweet, SecRoBERTa, ALBERT, RoBERTa) and four traditional machine learning classifiers (Random Forest, Multinomial Naïve Bayes, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine, using two encoders - Bag of Words and Term Frequency - Inverse Document Frequency), were trained to classify cyber incidents which were pseudonymised using Data Masking, Data Tokenisation and Data Substitution. The best-performing model attained an F1-score of 78.5% on the non-pseudonymised CECILIA-10C-900 dataset and 83% on the dataset, which was pseudonymised using Data Masking, D-CECILIA-10C-900-MAS. Therefore, this research demonstrates that it is possible for a single AI model to balance enhanced privacy with strong threat intelligence analysis capabilities.

title: Graph-based density-variation outlier removal for chronic disease prediction: A leakage-free benchmark and component-wise ablation
abstract: Chronic diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and heart disease impose a major global health burden. Machine-learning prediction systems offer valuable early-diagnostic support, but their performance is often degraded by outliers and class imbalance in real-world clinical tabular data. The standard remedy, DBSCAN, requires manual ε-tuning and assumes globally uniform density — assumptions that rarely hold on heterogeneous medical data. The recent AutoSCAN method removes the manual ε but has been validated only on synthetic clustering benchmarks, not on downstream medical classification. We propose YadroSeg, an extension of the graph-based coring framework of Le et al. [ 1 ], originally introduced for image segmentation, and adapted here to tabular medical data. YadroSeg builds a k-nearest-neighbour weighted graph and analyses a heap-based density variation sequence to identify noisy samples in an adaptive, parameter-free manner, using a novel geometric elbow criterion for automatic threshold selection. The cleaned data are then balanced with SMOTE-ENN and classified by a Random Forest. On five public chronic-disease datasets — diabetes, hypertension, CKD, Cleveland and Statlog heart disease — under 10-fold cross-validation, YadroSeg attains the best F1 on three datasets, reaching 98.87%. On the remaining two, YadroSeg-Grid and AutoSCAN are best, the latter benefiting from full data retention combined with SMOTE-ENN. These results confirm that graph-theoretic density analysis provides a mathematically principled and practically effective approach to noise filtering in imbalanced clinical tabular data.

evidence.title: Graph-based density-variation outlier removal for chronic disease prediction: A leakage-free benchmark and component-wise ablation
evidence.abstract: Chronic diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and heart disease impose a major global health burden. Machine-learning prediction systems offer valuable early-diagnostic support, but their performance is often degraded by outliers and class imbalance in real-world clinical tabular data. The standard remedy, DBSCAN, requires manual ε-tuning and assumes globally uniform density — assumptions that rarely hold on heterogeneous medical data. The recent AutoSCAN method removes the manual ε but has been validated only on synthetic clustering benchmarks, not on downstream medical classification. We propose YadroSeg, an extension of the graph-based coring framework of Le et al. [ 1 ], originally introduced for image segmentation, and adapted here to tabular medical data. YadroSeg builds a k-nearest-neighbour weighted graph and analyses a heap-based density variation sequence to identify noisy samples in an adaptive, parameter-free manner, using a novel geometric elbow criterion for automatic threshold selection. The cleaned data are then balanced with SMOTE-ENN and classified by a Random Forest. On five public chronic-disease datasets — diabetes, hypertension, CKD, Cleveland and Statlog heart disease — under 10-fold cross-validation, YadroSeg attains the best F1 on three datasets, reaching 98.87%. On the remaining two, YadroSeg-Grid and AutoSCAN are best, the latter benefiting from full data retention combined with SMOTE-ENN. These results confirm that graph-theoretic density analysis provides a mathematically principled and practically effective approach to noise filtering in imbalanced clinical tabular data.

title: Deep learning from the crowd Fundamentals of morphological galaxy classification
abstract: Aims. The objective of this work is to adapt a deep neural network model to perform galaxy morphological classification trained from crowd annotations, considering the training scheme, the agreement between the annotators, and the hierarchy. Methods. We use Galaxy Zoo 1 as our experimental testbed and trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) for the automatic classification of galaxies' morphologies. We analyze the impact of the following aspects on the classification accuracy and training efficiency: (i) Training only the last layer vs. training all the network; (ii) Classification with only the CNN vs. considering the hierarchy; (iii) Comparing the models trained with different amounts of data and levels of agreement between the annotators; (iv) Training by stages, transferring knowledge from one model to another; and (v) Combining several models as an ensemble. Results From the experiments, we derive the following results: (i) Training all the layers in the network significantly improves the accuracy (10% increase in exact match), compared to training only the last layer; (ii) There is a tradeoff between the amount of data and the level of agreement between the annotators used for training; (iii) Using the hierarchy can improve accuracy when the amount of training data is reduced; (iv) Training by stages through transfer learning (curriculum learning) produces higher accuracy for limited data; (v) Ensembles can improve accuracy; (vi) Models achieve a low accuracy for the most difficult cases, but, if we consider hierarchical measures, we can derive useful results for upper levels in the hierarchy. An accuracy above 99% is achieved when training all layers of the network and considering a high agreement between the annotators. Conclusions. Training deep learning models from crowd annotations involves additional challenges than learning from hard annotations.

title: The Adaptive Learning Framework Based on Graph-Based Machine Learning
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive learning framework for machine learning that automatically adjusts model parameters to enhance model performance. Traditional machine learning methods often lack the ability to dynamically adjust parameters based on data, limiting their effectiveness. This work introduces a novel approach leveraging graph structure to intelligently optimize model parameters, leading to improved accuracy and generalization. The framework employs a hierarchical graph representation to capture complex relationships within the data, facilitating automated parameter tuning. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through extensive experiments on various datasets, showcasing significant improvements in model performance compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism lies in the utilization of graph-based optimization techniques to systematically refine parameter values.

title: Quantum Entanglement Analysis and Anti-Decoy Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge to classical physics and has captivated researchers for decades. This paper investigates the concept of non-locality, specifically its connection to entanglement, and proposes a novel framework for analyzing quantum entanglement through a process called "Entanglement Anti-Decoy" (EAD). The core aim is to design an algorithm capable of reverse entanglement, offering a potential path towards quantum information processing. This research explores the implications of this approach, highlighting its potential to overcome the limitations of traditional quantum computation and provide a new avenue for exploring the mysteries of quantum entanglement. We will detail the proposed EAD algorithm, its underlying mathematical principles, and its potential to facilitate the development of robust quantum communication protocols. The paper will conclude with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this research.

abstract: Quantum particle physics simulation is a rapidly evolving field with the potential to revolutionize our understanding of fundamental physics. The core claim is that this framework will significantly advance our ability to explore the limits of quantum mechanics and potentially uncover new physics. The paper details the framework's design, implementation of key quantum algorithms, and preliminary results demonstrating the framework's effectiveness in simulating specific scenarios.
